steps.title: Confirm the decedent's principal residence status and the trust terms
steps.detail: Revocable trust transfer is excluded, but CIO occurs when the trust becomes irrevocable unless the trustor remains the sole present beneficiary. Distribution provisions (sprinkle powers) can affect exclusions.

steps.title: Obtain the parcel's tax bills and assessed value from the County Assessor
steps.detail: Reconcile client-provided history with bills (see irregularity IR01). Do not rely on unverified history.

steps.title: Decide whether the heir will move in (Prop 19 family home) or not
steps.detail: Move-in within one year and file homeowners' exemption within one year. Property B: only an owner-occupied unit qualifies.

steps.title: File the BOE-19-P (parent-child claim) within 3 years of transfer and before any third-party transfer
steps.detail: Failure to file on time can affect the exclusion and assessment timing.

steps.title: Estimate estate size against the federal basic exclusion ($15,000,000 in 2026)
steps.detail: Federal return threshold is based on the estate's total value. Two properties at client values are well below the 2026 figure; other assets matter.

steps.title: Heir's basis steps up to fair market value at death
steps.detail: Gain is measured from the date-of-death value. Keep appraisals and records.

steps.title: Hold, rent, or sell decision
steps.detail: Sale proceeds: county transfer tax $1.10 per $1,000 (city taxes unverified). Home-sale exclusion under section 121 may apply if the heir lives in the home 2 of 5 years.

steps.title: Plan for California income tax on income from inherited assets
steps.detail: Inheritance itself is not CA income. Rental income and investment gains are taxable. No state estate or inheritance tax.

steps.title: Plan for the 3.8% NIIT if investment or rental income exceeds thresholds
